articles.title: US Open: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to show the US Open until end of 2030
articles.summary: Sky Sports agrees three-year extension to broadcast the US Open; 2026 competition reaches thrilling conclusion at Flushing Meadows this weekend; watch Aryna Sabalenka take on Elena Rybakina in the women's final on Saturday, followed by the men's final on Sunday
articles.body:
As part of the partnership with the United States Tennis Association (USTA), Sky Sports will retain exclusive live coverage of all men's and women's singles, doubles, mixed doubles, juniors and wheelchair competitions throughout the three-week tournament. The agreement was negotiated by the USTA's media rights partner, IMG.

Alongside broadcast rights, fans in the UK and Ireland will also be able to catch up on all the action with clips and highlights available across Sky's digital and social platforms.

This year's coverage has featured augmented reality graphics, enhanced data integrations, in-depth touchscreen analysis and behind-the-scenes content, bringing fans closer to the action than ever before.

Sky's tennis coverage is led by presenter Gigi Salmon and includes expert analysis from Tim Henman and Laura Robson, alongside additional talent and co-commentators at events throughout the season. Match commentary is provided by Jonathan Overend.

The announcement comes amid a drama-filled US Open featuring the shock first-round exit of 24-time Grand Slam champion Novak Djokovic and the latest finish in tournament history between Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz as the American emerged victorious at 3.33am.

A thrilling women's final meanwhile awaits as World No 1 Aryna Sabalenka takes on World No 2 Elena Rybakina on Saturday.

Jonathan Licht, Chief Executive Officer Sky Sports UK & Ireland, said : "The US Open is one of the highlights of the sporting calendar, featuring the biggest names in both the men's and women's games, all set against the spectacular New York backdrop. We're delighted to extend our partnership with the USTA, reinforcing our shared commitment to embracing innovation, showcasing the best in the sport and delivering world-class coverage for viewers. This renewal further cements Sky Sports' position as the home of sport in the UK and Ireland, offering fans unrivalled breadth and value all year round."

Kirsten Corio, Chief Commercial Officer, USTA: "The US Open and Sky Sports have been trusted partners for many years, and we're excited to continue such a strong relationship with this renewal. Sky shares our commitment to delivering innovative and cutting-edge coverage to a great audience of tennis fans in the U.K. and Ireland, and we're confident that our continued partnership will have a direct impact on tennis' extraordinary growth and deepen fans' connection with the game."

Live tennis is available all year on Sky, including full coverage of the ATP and WTA Tours on Sky Sports or available to stream with NOW and the Sky Sports app. Sky Sports will broadcast over 4,000 matches and 80 tournaments this season.

The partnership extension adds to Sky's already unrivalled portfolio in the UK and Ireland with more top-quality sport than anywhere else, with most sport rights renewed until near the end of the decade. That includes 1,500 games from the Premier League, WSL, EFL and SPFL, exclusive live coverage from every Formula 1 race weekend until the end of 2034, home men's and women's international England cricket, every shot from the golf Majors, year-round coverage of darts, world class boxing from promoters Zuffa and MVP, and more action from the NFL, Netball Super League and rugby league.

The US Open is live on Sky Sports from August 30. Stream tennis with no contract on NOW and the Sky Sports App . You can also watch the Laver Cup at The O2 in London from 25-27 September live on Sky Sports.

articles.title: Los precios de las semifinales del US Open se desploman sin Carlos Alcaraz: ¡19 dólares!
articles.standfirst: El partido entre Zverev y Khachanov no ha despertado ninguna atención en Nueva York
articles.summary: El partido entre Zverev y Khachanov no ha despertado ninguna atención en Nueva York
articles.body: Las primeras consecuencias de la ausencia de Carlos Alcaraz en el cuadro individual masculino del US Open (el murciano cayó derrotado el martes en los cuartos con Ben Shelton) se empiezan a notar este viernes en las semifinales. Las entradas, que inicialmente tenían un precio de 300 dólares, se pueden adquirir en diferentes plataformas por tan sólo 19 dólares. Y es que la primera semifinal entre Alexander Zverev y Karen Khachanov no ha despertado ningún tipo de interés entre el público neoyorquino (antes se había jugado la fina de dobles femeninos) y ha dejado vacía la grada de la central Arthur Ashe, la pista más grande del mundo con capacidad para más de 20.000 espectadores. La ciudad de Nueva York vive de espaldas al tenis este viernes, no en vano se está celebrando el vigésimo quinto aniversario del atentado terrorista contra las Torres Gemelas. La Zona Cero cuenta en la actualidad con dos inmensas fuentes con cascadas artificiales situadas exactamente donde se erigían las torres. Se conmemora la fecha con la lectura pública de los nombres de los fallecidos. Estuvieron expresidentes de los Estados Unidos como Bush, Clinton, Obama y Biden. Faltó el actual, Donald Trump. El último grande del curso empezó poniendo a la venta las entradas más cara en la historia de los Grand Slam. El abono más barato de paseo, sin acceso a los estadios, ascendía a 323 dólares.

images.caption: La pista Arthur Ashe prácticamente vacía.

articles.title: US Open 2026 results: Taylor Townsend and Katerina Siniakova win women's doubles for career Grand Slam
articles.summary: Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend win the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam.
articles.body:
Katerina Siniakova and Taylor Townsend won the women's doubles at the US Open to complete a historic career doubles Grand Slam as a pairing.

The top seeds came from a set down to beat American wildcards Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7 6-0 6-2 in New York.

Their triumph at Flushing Meadows means they have now won all four Grand Slam titles, adding to their triumphs at Wimbledon in 2024, the Australian Open in 2025 and this year's French Open.

It was Czech player Siniakova's 12th Grand Slam doubles title in total, while she also became the first player to complete the career Slam with two different partners.

The 30-year-old achieved it previously with fellow Czech Barbora Krejcikova.

For American Townsend, who is also 30, victory marks her first US Open doubles title after suffering defeat in the final last year alongside Siniakova to Gabriela Dabrowski and Erin Routliffe.

Siniakova and Townsend had not dropped a set before the final, but lost the opener when the Czech player double-faulted three times in the final game.

They hit back in the second set, winning 23 of 27 points after the first game to force a decider.

Siniakova and Townsend remained in control from there, consolidating an early break in the third set to go 3-1 up before safely seeing out the rest of the match.

Siniakova is one of only eight women to have won at least 12 Grand Slam doubles titles in the Open era.

Should Siniakova end this season as the world number one in doubles, it will mark the sixth time she has achieved the feat, surpassing Martina Navratilova for the most year-end top-ranked finishes in WTA history.

images.caption: Image caption, Taylor Townsend (left) and Katerina Siniakova have won four Grand Slam doubles titles together

articles.title: Townsend, Siniakova win US Open women's doubles title for career Grand Slam
articles.summary: It was a double celebration for Katerina Siniakova and for Taylor Townsend, the final piece of the puzzle to a career Grand Slam.
articles.body:
NEW YORK – It was a double celebration for Katerina Siniakova and for Taylor Townsend, the final piece of the puzzle to a career Grand Slam.

Siniakova and Townsend, the tournament's No. 1 seed, captured their first U.S. Open women's doubles title together, rallying to beat young Americans Ashlyn Krueger and Robin Montgomery 5-7, 6-0, 6-2 in the final in Arthur Ashe Stadium on on Friday, Sept. 11.

Townsend, a 30 year-old American, and Siniakova, a 30-year-old from Czechia, captured their first major title at Wimbledon in 2024 before adding the 2025 Australian Open, the 2026 French Open and this US Open championship.

Townsend and Siniakova found themselves down 0-3, and went on to lose the first set, but then they turned it on, blanking the wildcard entrants in the second set, before slamming and forehand baselining their way to a 6-2 closing set.

For Siniakova, it was actually the second time she completed career doubles Grand Slam, having already accomplished the feat with Barbora Krejcikova when the pair won the 2022 US Open. She has also won a doubles title at the 2024 French Open with Coco Gauff.

"There was lot of nerves," Siniakova said after the match. "We were really fighting for this one, so I'm just really proud. We did it."

Krueger and Montgomery went on quite a run, beating the defending champions Erin Routliffe and Gabriela Dabrowski in separate matches, as both played with different partners this time around.

It was also a reunion for Krueger and Montgomery, who won the U.S. Open girls' doubles title in 2021.

"I think with what we've just done has been amazing." Montgomery said. "I think we did forget that we were offered a wild card, so I'm just glad we made good use of it, and I'm glad we were able to come back together and continue playing here, especially with our success in juniors."

For Townsend, the match served a greater historical marker for black American tennis players. Addressing the fans inside Ashe following their victory, Townsend pointed out that there were two Black American women competing in the doubles final – herself and Montgomery – on the same day two Black American men will face off in the men's singles semifinals for a place in Sunday's final.

Watch: Townsend and Siniakova celebrate with bottles of bubbly

articles.title: US Open men's semifinals: Score, live updates as Alexander Zverev, Karen Khachanov open play, followed by all-American showdown between Ben Shelton, Frances Tiafoe
articles.summary: With the final four set, a first-time US Open champion is officially guaranteed.
articles.body: The 2026 US Open continues Friday with two men's semifinal matches that will decide Sunday afternoon's final, the last Grand Slam title of the year.No. 1 seed Alexander Zverev and unseeded Karen Khachanov will open up play, as Zverev bids for a second major title of the season after breaking through at Roland-Garros in June for his first career Grand Slam crown. He steamrolled Netherlands' Botic van de Zandschulp in Wednesday's quarterfinal and will look to carry that momentum into Friday's match against Khachanov, who is still seeking his first career Grand Slam final appearance.The night session brings the match of the day: No. 8 seed Ben Shelton and No. 11 seed Frances Tiafoe in an all-American semifinal at 7 p.m. ET — just the second all-American men's Grand Slam semifinal since 2005. Whoever survives will be one win away from becoming the first American man to claim a major since Andy Roddick in 2003. This evening's match will have a lot to live up to following Wednesday's quarterfinal between Shelton and defending champion Carlos Alcaraz — a grueling four-and-a-half-hour match in which Shelton managed the biggest win of his career as the final shot landed … at 3:33 a.m.Where to watch US Open men's semifinalsAlexander Zverev-Karen Khachanov start time: 3 p.m. ETBen Shelton-Frances Tiafoe start time: No earlier than 7 p.m. ETLocation: Arthur Ashe Stadium | Queens, N.Y.TV channel/live stream: ESPNFollow along with Yahoo Sports for the latest highlights, news and more from the 2026 US Open men's semifinals.
